metadata.quote: Aramco operates in an industry characterized by market volatility, hazardous operations, and uncertain project outcomes.

disclosures.title: Crude oil supply, demand and price exposure
disclosures.body_text: Crude oil sales are Aramco's largest revenue component, so international supply, demand and sale prices can materially change operating results and cash flow.

metadata.quote: Aramco’s results of operations and cash flow are significantly impacted by international crude oil supply and demand and the price at which it sells crude oil.

disclosures.title: Asian demand and political concentration
disclosures.body_text: A substantial portion of crude, refined and chemical exports goes to Asian customers; adverse regional economic or political developments could reduce demand and increase competition.

metadata.quote: In 2025 and 2024, customers in Asia, including Company’s affiliated refineries located in Asia, purchased 82% and 81%, respectively, of its crude oil exports.

disclosures.title: Climate transition and net-zero execution
disclosures.body_text: Climate policy, regulation, litigation, investor preferences and substitution may reduce hydrocarbon demand or capital access, while the 2050 Scope 1 and 2 net-zero ambition may require substantial capital and may not be fully achieved.

metadata.quote: Aramco may incur substantial costs and capital expenditures to achieve its net-zero ambition. In addition, Aramco may not fully meet its announced net-zero ambition by 2050.

disclosures.title: Global crude, refining and petrochemical competition
disclosures.body_text: Competitive pressure from national and international oil companies and from refining and petrochemical capacity in served markets can reduce prices, market share and downstream profitability.

metadata.quote: Competitive pressure could have a material adverse impact on the price at which it sells crude oil and other products.

disclosures.title: Operational incidents and critical-asset concentration
disclosures.body_text: Spills, leaks, fires, equipment failure, transportation disruption and natural disasters can harm people and the environment, interrupt operations and create liabilities; key Saudi processing and transport assets increase disruption exposure.

metadata.quote: Aramco is subject to operational risks and hazards that may have a significant impact on its operations or result in significant liabilities and costs.

disclosures.title: Capital-project delivery and return risk
disclosures.body_text: Growth depends on timely and cost-effective project delivery. Funding, permits, contractors, regulation, technology and market assumptions can cause delays, cost overruns, impairments or returns below plan.

metadata.quote: Aramco’s ability to achieve its strategic growth objectives depends on the successful delivery of current and future projects

disclosures.title: Insurance coverage limitations
disclosures.body_text: Aramco primarily self-insures through its captive insurer and does not insure every risk or maintain business-interruption cover for disruptions, creating potential exposure to significant uninsured losses.

metadata.quote: Aramco does not insure against all risks and its insurance may not protect it against liability from all potential events

disclosures.title: Terrorism and armed-conflict exposure
disclosures.body_text: Past attacks affected facilities and temporarily reduced production. Additional attacks or armed conflict could disrupt operations, require significant spending and affect the share price.

metadata.quote: Additional terrorist or other attacks or armed conflict could impact Aramco’s operations and have a material adverse effect

disclosures.title: Hydrocarbon reserve-estimation uncertainty
disclosures.body_text: Proved-reserve estimates depend on interpretations, assumptions, judgments, economic conditions and commercial viability; new information, price changes, regulation or errors can reduce estimated quantity or value.

metadata.quote: Estimates of proved hydrocarbon reserves depend on significant interpretations, assumptions, and judgments.

disclosures.title: IT systems and cybersecurity exposure
disclosures.body_text: Critical information and operational technology supports production, records and communications. Aramco is a high-profile cyber target; it reported that attempts had not been material to financial performance or reputation to date, while future attacks could cause physical, environmental, legal and financial harm.

metadata.quote: Aramco’s systems are a high-profile target for sophisticated cyberattacks by nation states, and criminal hackers

disclosures.title: Antitrust, climate and trade litigation exposure
disclosures.body_text: Aramco reports significant litigation exposure primarily in the United States and Saudi Arabia, including OPEC-related antitrust claims, climate and greenwashing claims, and trade measures affecting exports. Existing OPEC-related cases had been dismissed on sovereign defenses, but future outcomes are not assured.

metadata.quote: Aramco is and has been subject to significant litigation, primarily in the United States and the Kingdom.

disclosures.title: Government licences, permits and concession dependency
disclosures.body_text: Operations depend on maintaining the Concession and licences, permits and approvals under the Hydrocarbons Law, Energy Supply Law and laws of other jurisdictions. Failure, revocation or termination could interrupt operations and cause penalties.

metadata.quote: Aramco is required to obtain, maintain, and renew Governmental licenses, permits, and approvals in order to operate its businesses.

disclosures.title: Liquidity management and contractual maturities
disclosures.body_text: Aramco manages liquidity through cash and cash equivalents, available credit facilities, cash-flow forecasts and liquid investments. Security and liquidity are prioritized over yield, and borrowings are monitored by contractual maturity.

metadata.quote: Saudi Aramco’s liquidity risk management includes maintaining sufficient cash and cash equivalents and ensuring the availability of incremental funding through credit facilities
